references.text: The parallel passage in [ref:Matt 10:27|Matthew 10:27], where Jesus says, "What I tell you in the dark, speak in the light; and what is whispered in your ear, proclaim from the housetops." This is the closest parallel to Luke 12:3, but with a slightly different emphasis—in Matthew, Jesus encourages his disciples to preach openly, while in Luke it concerns how what is hidden will inevitably be revealed.

In [ref:Luk 8:17|Luke 8:17], Jesus says, "For nothing is hidden that will not be made manifest, nor anything secret that will not be known and come to light." This underscores the same principle as in Luke 12:3—that everything hidden will eventually be revealed.

[ref:Mark 4:22|Mark 4:22] expresses the same principle: "For there is nothing hidden except that it should be made manifest, nor anything secret except that it should come to light." This confirms the theme that all secrets will be brought into the light.

[ref:Fork 12:14|Ecclesiastes 12:14] speaks of God judging every deed, including everything hidden, whether good or evil. This supports the idea in Luke 12:3 that nothing remains hidden from God's judgment.

[ref:Job 12:22|Job 12:22] says that God "reveals the deep and dark places and brings death's shadow into the light." This is an Old Testament basis for God revealing what is hidden in darkness, which connects to Luke 12:3.

[ref:1 Kor 4:5|1 Corinthians 4:5] speaks of the Lord bringing to light what is hidden in darkness and exposing the motives of hearts when he comes. Here Paul confirms the same principle that Jesus teaches in Luke 12:3.
[ref:Rom 2:16|Romans 2:16] speaks of the day when God will judge the secrets of people. This supports the idea in Luke 12:3 that what is said in secret will be revealed.

The immediate context in [ref:Luk 12:2|Luke 12:2] says, "Nothing is covered up that will not be revealed, and nothing hidden that will not be made known." Verse 3 expands and specifies this principle by mentioning what is said in the dark and whispered in the innermost room.

[ref:Jes 29:15|Isaiah 29:15] pronounces a "woe" on those who hide their plans from the Lord and do their deeds in darkness, saying, "Who sees us? Who knows us?" God reveals that nothing can be hidden from him, which aligns with the message of Luke 12:3.
